Title: Export memory stays bounded for a large asset
Preconditions: A fixture asset of at least 200 MB attached to a product; a way to observe platform memory
Steps:
1. [STATUS] Record baseline platform working-set and managed-heap before the export
2. [ADMIN] Create a backup with Binary enabled including the large asset
3. [STATUS] Sample platform memory at short intervals during the export
4. [MATH] Compare the peak memory delta against the asset size
Assertions:
{OBSERVED} Five back-to-back binary exports pushed 900 MiB of incompressible assets (deflate ratio 1.0003) in 3.5 minutes; the executing pod went 559 -> 559 MiB with a peak excursion of about 4 MiB, while buffering would have reached ~1.4 GiB by run 5.
{OBSERVED} No OutOfMemoryException and no container restart; the pod also fell back from its peak (563 -> 553 -> 559 MiB), showing the plateau is retained GC heap plus page cache rather than a leak.
Cross_Layer_Checks: Grafana workload vcptcore-qa1-platform, per-pod series (two replicas; a deployment average would halve the spike). 4 GiB limit at ~520-560 MiB usage, so an OOM was never the detector — the graph delta is.
Failure_Signals: Memory delta approximates or exceeds the asset size; OOM; container OOMKilled; export times out
References: VCST-5387; story goal of bounded predictable memory; QA step 11 of comment 2026-08-11; Verified: VCST-5387 (2026-08-19, vcptcore-qa1)

Title: A fully clean restore deletes its source backup from storage
Preconditions: A backup present in the storage backups folder, produced by an export rather than uploaded
Steps:
1. [HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/assets?folderUrl=backups and confirm the backup is listed
2. [ADMIN] Restore from that stored backup and let it finish with zero errors
3. [HTTP] List the backups folder again
4. [ADMIN] Repeat with a backup whose restore reports at least one error (for example one containing the invalid NFC_ product) and list the folder again
Assertions:
{OBSERVED} After a restore that finished with errors=0 the source backup is GONE from the backups folder — verified with a controlled run: present before, absent after, and a later download of the same name returns 404.
{SPEC} After a restore that recorded ANY error the backup is KEPT, so the operator can retry without re-uploading — the deletion is guarded by pushNotification.Errors.Count == 0.
Cross_Layer_Checks: The Restore blade storage listing no longer offers the consumed backup on refresh
Failure_Signals: A backup deleted even though the restore reported errors (the operator loses the ability to retry); a backup kept after a clean restore contradicting the documented behaviour
References: src: https://github.com/VirtoCommerce/vc-module-backup-restore BackupRestoreController — "Drop the uploaded backup only on a fully clean restore"; Verified: VCST-5387 (2026-08-20, vcptcore-qa1)

Title: A cancelled backup is presented as finished and offers its partial archive for download
Preconditions: Admin on the Data backup blade; a selection large enough that the run lasts long enough to cancel (Select all works)
Steps:
1. [ADMIN] Select all, Start backup, and cancel it partway through
2. [ADMIN] Read the progress header, the footer, and whether a download is offered
3. [ADMIN] Open Backup storage and read the size of the produced file
4. [ADMIN] Expand a failed module and read the per-module error
Assertions:
{OBSERVED} The header reads "Backup finished" — the SAME wording a successful run produces — with a Start/End range. Nothing in the header or the timestamps says the job was cancelled.
{OBSERVED} A "Download backup" link is offered for the partial archive, and the archive is real: 93 MB, containing the 6 platform sections and 6 modules that completed, while 20 modules are error rows. Restoring it would restore a silent subset.
{OBSERVED} The only differentiating signal is the footer "Completed with errors", which reads as a failure rather than as an operator-initiated cancel; the per-module errors do say "The operation was canceled." but only after expanding a row. Evidence: screenshots/BKRS-036-cancel-reads-as-finished.png
Cross_Layer_Checks: The partial archive appears in Backup storage indistinguishable from a complete one — same naming, no partial marker
Failure_Signals: A cancelled run that leaves no trace at all; a partial archive that restores without reporting the missing modules. NOTE this case records the CURRENT behaviour so a change is detected; the open question — whether a cancelled run should be labelled cancelled and whether its partial output should be offered as a backup at all — is carried in the ticket report, not asserted here
Cleanup: Delete the partial archive from Backup storage
References: src: https://github.com/VirtoCommerce/vc-module-backup-restore; Verified: VCST-5387 (2026-08-20, vcptcore-qa1, Chromium admin SPA)
